title: From Dead-End to Conversion
summary: Redesigning the reactivation flow so returning Boost Mobile customers are guided back in instead of hitting a dead end.

sections.label: OVERVIEW
sections.title: Resolving edge case friction using design system components.
sections.body: Returning users are highly valuable, yet our existing system treated them like strangers who took a wrong turn. When a previous user attempted to reactivate their service, they were met with a hard roadblock: a generic error message offering no next steps, no login redirect, and no explanation.

sections.label: PROBLEM
sections.title: Deactivated users attempting to reactivate their account are met with a roadblock.
sections.body: This dead-end experience caused immediate friction, likely leading to high drop-off rates and abandonment. The goal was to redesign the reactivation flow to gracefully guide returning users back into the ecosystem, no matter their account status.

sections.label: SOLUTION
sections.title: Different paths lead to different outcomes.
sections.body: The PM on this project provided 4 flows with distinct technical scenarios. I drove the direction on which design system component to implement given each context.

mediaBlocks.caption: Global notification
mediaBlocks.body: Provide context to the user for their lack of eligibility.

mediaBlocks.caption: Interstitial
mediaBlocks.body: Some context requires a hard stop with an immediate opportunity for resolution.

mediaBlocks.caption: Modal
mediaBlocks.body: Give users an easy way out of the create account flow with a redirection.

sections.label: PROCESS
sections.title: Iteration through technical constraints.
sections.body: The PM and TPMs provided additional considerations for design through weekly sprints. The User flows iterated along with my product deliverables until reaching a final version.

images.alt: User flow diagram for returning, existing and ineligible customers

sections.label: OUTCOME
sections.title: Handoff & Implementation.
sections.body:
By replacing a dead-end error with actionable, contextual pathways, the new flow transforms friction into retention. Users are no longer abandoned at the door; they are actively guided back inside. A generic "Error 404" or "Action Failed" does not help anyone. Telling the user why an action failed and how to fix it is the cornerstone of trust.

To eliminate ambiguity during implementation, I leveraged Figma Dev Mode to structure the final handoff. By meticulously connecting component states, spacing variables, and logic for each edge case directly within the dev interface, the engineering team was equipped with build-ready specs that accelerated deployment.
